title: Minimum Total Price After Applying Discounts
summary: Given integer arrays prices and discounts, where prices[i] is the price of the i-th item and discounts[j] is a discount percentage, determine the minimum total price after applying at most one discount to each item.
statement: Given integer arrays prices and discounts, where prices[i] is the price of the i-th item and discounts[j] is a discount percentage, determine the minimum total price after applying at most one discount to each item. Each discount reduces the price by the given percentage, and no item can receive more than one discount. The final price is calculated as (price * (100 - discount)) / 100 without rounding. The goal is to assign discounts optimally to achieve the lowest total price, with answers within 10^-5 of the actual value being acceptable.
constraints: Apply each percentage discount to at most one item and at most one discount per item.
Unused discounts and undiscounted items are allowed.
Return the minimum unrounded total price.
hints: Maximize savings by sorting both prices and discounts descending and pairing corresponding positions.
Leave excess prices undiscounted and excess discounts unused.
The rearrangement inequality proves like-ranked pairing maximizes total savings.
editorial: The rearrangement inequality proves like-ranked pairing maximizes total savings.

tests.explanation: Pair sixty percent with thirty and fifty percent with twenty-one, leaving ten, for total 32.5.
Use the larger fifty-percent discount on the only item, paying five.
